extracted.intended_audience: public relations and communications practitioners (PR pros, corporate communicators, agency staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidelines for when and how to write and distribute press releases, evaluated through the PESO (Paid, Earned, Shared, Owned) framework and Spin Sucks' PR principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: PESO Model (Paid, Earned, Shared, Owned)
rubrics_metrics.description: P: Paid — Sponsored content, ads, paid placements; E: Earned — Traditional media coverage from pitches; S: Shared — Social media engagement and sharing; O: Owned — Your blog, newsroom, newsletter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PESO as a framework to plan amplification and to evaluate how a release will perform across channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release fits primarily as Earned media
rubrics_metrics.description: Earned media tactic primarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize newsworthiness and media angles that reporters will pick up rather than treating the release as an advertisement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release can serve as Owned content
rubrics_metrics.description: Owned: if posted to your newsroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing the release on your own channels (newsroom, blog, newsletter) ensures discoverability and provides a canonical source for links and SEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases should be amplifiable through Shared channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Can be amplified through Shared (social media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare social assets and messaging to encourage sharing and to increase reach beyond earned placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use press releases as Paid placements
rubrics_metrics.description: Should NOT be Paid (loses credibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid distributing releases as paid ads or native sponsorships that undermine journalistic credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: News should cross 2+ PESO categories
rubrics_metrics.description: What Makes a Press Release Worth Writing: News that crosses 2+ PESO categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize releases that can be activated across multiple channels (e.g., earned pickup + owned content + social sharing) to justify the effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release should provide material for owned content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides material for blog posts (Owned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the release contains enough substance, data, quotes, or assets to spawn follow-up owned content (blog posts, analyses, newsletters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Release should be shareable on social
rubrics_metrics.description: Worth sharing on social (Shared).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think about social angles, headlines, visuals, and easy excerpts to increase the likelihood of social amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release must have an angle journalists will pick up
rubrics_metrics.description: Has an angle media will pick up (Earned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a clear news hook or reporter-focused angle; if there is no plausible earned-media hook, reconsider issuing a release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency over manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Spin Sucks 'PR Manifesto' principle: Transparency over manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be honest and open in releases; avoid spin or misleading framing that could damage long-term trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationships over transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Spin Sucks 'PR Manifesto' principle: Relationships over transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write releases and outreach with the aim of building journalist and stakeholder relationships rather than chasing one-off hits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance over style
rubrics_metrics.description: Spin Sucks 'PR Manifesto' principle: Substance over style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize meaningful content, data, and context over flashy language or jargon-filled marketing copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term reputation over short-term coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Spin Sucks 'PR Manifesto' principle: Long-term reputation over short-term coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess releases for reputational impact and avoid tactical releases that could harm credibility later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement over assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Spin Sucks 'PR Manifesto' principle: Measurement over assumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set measurable goals and track outcomes (media pickups, engagement, conversions) rather than assuming success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will it create conversation or just announcements?
rubrics_metrics.description: Press Release Quality Test: Will it create conversation or just announcements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer releases that prompt discussion, commentary, or further content rather than mere informational posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has a clear 'so what?' for the reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Press Release Quality Test: Does it have a 'so what?' answer for the reader?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every release should answer: why should the audience care? If you can't articulate that, don't issue it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can be excerpted by other media
rubrics_metrics.description: Press Release Quality Test: Can it be excerpted by other media?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quotable lines, key data points, and a clear lede so journalists can easily repurpose content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will remain relevant in 6 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Press Release Quality Test: Will it still be relevant in 6 months?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor releases with enduring relevance when possible; avoid ephemeral announcements unless timing is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advances the brand narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Press Release Quality Test: Does it advance our brand narrative?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each release ties back to an overarching brand story or strategy rather than being isolated promotional noise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid marketing puffery ('leading provider of solutions')
rubrics_metrics.description: Common Anti-Pattern: 'Leading provider of solutions' — generic, promotional language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove platitudes and unsupported superlatives; use concrete facts and evidence instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid boilerplate excitement phrases ('We are excited to announce')
rubrics_metrics.description: Common Anti-Pattern: 'We are excited to announce' opening lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with news value, not internal enthusiasm; use an informative lede rather than formulaic client-speak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not let releases read like advertisements
rubrics_metrics.description: Common Anti-Pattern: Press releases that read like advertisements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the tone journalistic and factual; focus on newsworthiness rather than product marketing copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid quotes from executives who didn't review them
rubrics_metrics.description: Common Anti-Pattern: Quotes from executives who didn't review the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure quoted spokespeople have reviewed and approved their quotes to avoid inaccuracies and embarrassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time releases with the news cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Common Anti-Pattern: Releases timed without consideration of news cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider competing news, embargoes, and reporter availability when scheduling distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include multimedia (photos, video, infographics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern Best Practice: Multimedia (photos, video, infographics) required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality images, video, or graphics to increase pickup, social sharing, and newsroom usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile-first formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern Best Practice: Mobile-first formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format releases and associated landing pages for mobile consumption (short paragraphs, clear headings, fast-loading assets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a social media kit with the release
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern Best Practice: Social media kit accompanying release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include suggested posts, visuals sized for platforms, hashtags, and speaker handles to ease sharing by journalists and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief internal stakeholders before release
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern Best Practice: Internal stakeholders briefed before release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure spokespeople and internal teams are prepared for media inquiries and social reaction to avoid mixed messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track analytics on the release landing page
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern Best Practice: Analytics tracking on landing page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement tracking (UTMs, page analytics) to measure traffic, engagement, conversions, and channels driving results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worth-doing test passed
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric (Spin Sucks): Worth-doing test passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A summary gate: only issue releases that pass the 'worth doing' criteria (newsworthiness, cross-channel potential, audience value).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance over hype / substance over style
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric: Substance over hype.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure releases contain meaningful content (data, context, implications) rather than hype or promotional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia included (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric: Multimedia included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multimedia is a required checklist item: photos, video, infographics should be attached or linked for newsroom use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-PESO amplification planned
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric: Cross-PESO amplification planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a concrete plan for how the release will be amplified across Earned, Owned, and Shared channels (and avoid Paid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent and honest (quality rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric: Transparent and honest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid misleading claims; provide sources and verifiable facts to preserve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversation-starter, not just announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric: Conversation-starter, not just announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for releases that provoke discussion, generate commentary, or enable follow-up stories rather than being static notices.
